explanation:
[EFFECT]
The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, bimodal effect on predicted bike demand. Demand is at its lowest in the very early morning, with contributions bottoming out around 4–5 a.m. (roughly –3 in log space, meaning a very large multiplier downward). It then rises sharply to a first peak at 8 a.m. (morning commute), dips slightly through mid-morning, stays moderately positive through the afternoon, and reaches its highest point at 17–18 (the evening commute, ~+1.2–1.3 in log space). After 18:00, contributions gradually decline, turning slightly negative again by midnight.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9, with an importance score of 0.889. Its contribution spans a range of roughly 4 log units from trough to peak, making it by far the strongest driver of predicted demand.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Bike availability and staffing should be concentrated around the two daily demand peaks — approximately 8 a.m. and 5–6 p.m. — while overnight coverage (especially 1–6 a.m.) can be scaled back significantly to match the very low predicted demand during those hours.
